IPT.evidence_source: [/page/0/Text/7] For several years, we have been exploring the efficacy of self-administered cognitive therapy for depression. The original investigations were with depressed older adult participants involved in what we chose to call cognitive bibliotherapy (Scogin, Hamblin, & Beutler, 1987; Scogin, Jamison, & Gochneaur, 1989). This treatment consisted of reading Feeling Good (Burns 1980), a self-administered version of cognitive therapy for depression, and receiving weekly monitoring telephone calls from a researcher associated with the project.
